rung_why: cost is a tie (3.9% spread across rungs, band 10%), so the tie-break is the one yield column where the rungs separate: one-per-cluster class-4 rate

cspacing_basis.adopted: 2026-08-03, Matt's decision. The measurement below sizes the choice; it does not make it — there is no knee to read a floor off (see `rule`).

supersedes.why: its pairs were rendered at their OWN viewports, so framing dissimilarity was scored as look dissimilarity and produced an apparent return-to-baseline at 1e-2. At a fixed viewport the same distance reads 0.354 near-dup on constructed pairs and 0.130 on the pool's own, against a 0.0036 baseline.

cspacing_basis.measured_on: 1421 c (14 regions x 63 satellites over 10 half-decade annuli 1e-5..3e-1, + the 539-c committed v2 pool) x 3 SHARED z-viewports = 4263 embeddings
cspacing_basis.recipe: library morph CLIP (robustz_tanh_k2_v1, 640x360ss2, vit_base_patch16_clip_224.openai) at cos >= 0.974
cspacing_basis.rule: a TOLERANCE against pool cost, not a saturation point: the near-dup rate decays smoothly over five decades and reaches the different-region baseline nowhere below ~3e-1, so no bucket boundary can be read as a knee
cspacing_basis.viewport_conditional: 0.354 (wide, fw 1.3) vs 0.130 (mid, fw 0.55) at 1e-2 on the same pairs; wide is the framing the class is emitted at, so wide is the read and it is the conservative one
cspacing_basis.dM_distance_split: 0.294 near dM vs 0.547 further out at 1e-2-3.2e-2, same direction in every bin; NOT adopted as a covariate rule — every channel selects onto the knife edge, which is the half this floor is set on
cspacing_basis.note: one c per ATOM is NOT sufficient: the roster's atoms sit a median 9.1e-4 apart, two decades inside the floor

note: first-wins thinning ACROSS channels in measured-yield order; the ordering is the policy. Re-thinned from the full merged candidate list, never from a previous pool file.
